title: Sensitive Data Exposure - Password Hash Exposure in GET /api/v1/users/:id
description: The GET /api/v1/users/:id endpoint in the vulnerable API returns a single user's data including the passwordHash field. The getUser use case returns a User entity which includes the passwordHash field (Argon2id hash). The vulnerable handler directly serializes the User entity to JSON without filtering out the passwordHash field, exposing the target user's password hash to any authenticated user who knows their user ID.
impact: Targeted password hash exfiltration. An authenticated attacker can retrieve the Argon2id password hash of any user by their ID via GET /api/v1/users/:id. Combined with IDOR (no ownership check on GET /users/:id), any authenticated user can extract the password hash of any other user including ADMINs. Argon2id hashes can be subjected to offline brute-force attacks (GPU: ~10k H/s per GPU).
mitigation: 1) Explicitly exclude passwordHash from user response DTOs in both list and single user endpoints. 2) Use a UserResponseDTO that explicitly defines allowed fields (id, name, email, role, status, createdAt, updatedAt) and excludes passwordHash. 3) Implement a UserResponseMapper or UserSerializer that explicitly defines the public API shape. 4) Secure API (api-secure) explicitly excludes passwordHash in response mapping.
